query: Why did hardware incidents spike in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: hardware_equipment_class
per_column.rationale: The class of hardware (system/printer/network) is a candidate cause whose distribution could explain why hardware incidents spiked; it is a plausible driver of the outcome surfaced from the data.

per_column.name: failure_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The failure mechanism (update_failure, connectivity_lost) is a direct candidate cause of the incident spike; e.g. a wave of update_failures could attribute the spike. This is the most direct treatment/cause variable.

per_column.name: recurrence_pattern
per_column.rationale: Describes whether incidents repeat; this is more a characterization/consequence of the spike than a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome. Closer to a descriptive marker of the outcome than a confounder.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Technician workload/skill can plausibly influence which failures get logged/resolved and correlate with incident counts, but its status as a genuine common cause of both a treatment and the outcome is weak; often it is downstream of the incident (a collider-ish assignment).

per_column.name: caller_identity
per_column.rationale: Certain callers/departments may use particular hardware and be more prone to report incidents, plausibly a common cause of both equipment class exposure and reporting of incidents; surfaced from data.

per_column.name: urgency_impact_level
per_column.rationale: Urgency/impact is a downstream consequence/severity rating assigned to an incident, on the effect side rather than a common cause; adjusting for it would be a mistake.

judge.rationale: The columns clearly supply candidate TREATMENTS (failure_mechanism, hardware_equipment_class) that could attribute the spike, and none of the confounders were named in the query. However, the set is weak on genuine CONFOUNDERS -- common causes of BOTH treatment and outcome. Notably absent is any temporal/exposure variable (e.g., rollout timing, patch/change events, volume/load) that would confound the anomaly-window attribution. The proposed confounders (caller_identity, assigned_technician) are only weakly plausible as common causes and lean toward downstream assignment/reporting, while urgency_impact_level and recurrence_pattern sit on the outcome/collider side. The operator set up a treatment but did not convincingly surface adjustment-worthy confounders, so causal attribution is only partially realised.
